title: People’s Mañanera September 21
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**600,000 Attend Presidential Report Assemblies  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum toured 26 states and brought together nearly
600,000 people. “These have been very good assemblies, with a lot of
enthusiasm. There have been nearly 600,000 people in total in all the
assemblies,” she noted.

**More Than 19 Million Students Receive Scholarships/Stipends  
** The Ministry of Public Education (SEP) reported that 19.5 million students
have received educational scholarships/stipends, and the number is expected to
reach 20.1 million. During the current administration, 8.5 million Rita Cetina
scholarships/stipends and 4.2 million Benito Juárez scholarships/stipends have
been awarded, among other forms of support.

**Mexico, Second-Highest Growth in the G20  
** Mexico’s GDP grew 1.4% in the second quarter of 2026. This is the second-
highest growth rate in the G20, trailing only India, according to figures
cited by the Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Sheinbaum noted the figure “for all those who say things are going very
badly.”

**Mexico Strengthens Its Diesel Supply  
** The Olmeca Refinery and the modernization of other refineries enable Mexico
to be self-sufficient in diesel and help keep prices in check. The President
emphasized that “if the Dos Bocas refinery didn’t exist, we would be facing
supply problems.”

**Mexico: Dialogue With the U.S. While Respecting Sovereignty  
** Mexico is engaged in dialogue with the United States regarding tariffs and
the review of the USMCA, defending its interests and national laws. On
security, Sheinbaum reiterated that “interference or intervention does not
strengthen national institutions. On the contrary, it weakens them.”
